# PERIODONTAL DISEASE

Periodontal disease, including gingivitis and periodontitis, may progress into more severe disease or cause hematogenous spreading of bacteria if left untreated. All patients with periodontal disease should be referred to the dental service for assessment and direction of treatment. In the presence of gingivitis, the most commonly isolated subgingival flora includes Prevotella intermedia, Capnocytophaga spp, Finegoldia magna and Peptostreptococcus. In the presence of periodontitis, flora increases in complexity to most commonly include Porphyromonas gingivalis, P. intermedia, Aggregatibacter actinomycetemcomitans, Tanneralla forsythensis and Treponema denticola.

Therapy:
## Severe periodontitis or acute complicated gingivitis (ulceration, rapidly advancing disease, severe pain, patients with immunocompromising conditions) treatment

Consult Dental Service.

## Non-severe periodontitis or acute simple gingivitis treatment

Chlorhexidine 0.12% oral rinse swish for 30 seconds, then spit 15 ml twice daily for 7 days ($) [M]
